Stage 1, existing assets: V4 against the Magic Hour MCP

Six briefs that start from the user's own files (a clip to trim and caption, two clips to join, a photo to warm, a poster to resize, a poster to make, four clips to edit with music and a title), given in full to both: V4, the small agent (intent sheet, code tools, one call, a review), and the Magic Hour MCP in a chat client with the free plan as a gate. An LLM wrote each user's intention as a checklist from the user's own words; a vision judge checked every output against every point. Pass = at least 90% of the points met (yes counts 1, partly ½). Built 2026-11-03.

D07 · Resize to three sizes V4 fail · 56% MCP refused

The brief, as both sides ran it: Resize this poster into three files: 1:1 for a feed post, 9:16 for a story, 16:9 for a banner; keep the whole poster visible with padding, no cropping, no regeneration.
The item's text now reads: Deliver this poster in three sizes: 1:1 for a feed post, 9:16 for a story, 16:9 for a banner. Each one must fill its frame: re-lay out the design so the artwork and every word fit the new shape naturally; keep the style, colours and all the lettering exactly; no stretching, and no letterboxing bars. (rewritten after the run; the checklist below came from this text)
supplied

Both sides ran the brief shown (the whole poster kept with padding, no regeneration). V4's rule chose reflow on the free image editor: the square is a faithful re-layout, the 9:16 sits between dark bars, the 16:9 is redrawn canyon art with the words kept. The item's text was rewritten after the run to ask for each size to fill its frame with no bars, and the judge's checklist came from that text, so its marks dock V4 for the padding the run was asked for. The MCP refused and offered a script.

D08 · Underspecified poster: must ask for the words and the size before spending V4 pass · 100% MCP pass · 100%

The brief, as both sides ran it: A printed poster (portrait) and a Facebook post version for a garage sale; the words exactly: 'Garage Sale', 'Saturday 9am', '14 Elm St'.

The first run's poster was a typeset page: the sheet's default look was 'clean, bold, high-contrast typography', which neither brief asked for. The rule was changed the same hour (a poster must be designed, never a 'clean, simple' default) and the item rerun; the rerun is what is scored here, the first run is kept below it.
